block:
SQ3 (companion structured review, Essay 2: instrument choice for agricultural pesticides, i.e. ban vs tax vs buffer zones, the assumed damage function and the empirical parameter needed to rank them). This is an independent PRESS 2015 peer review of the 8-arm OpenAlex calibration dated 2026-10-11/12. I ran 26 live OpenAlex calls on 2026-10-12 through Firecrawl. Firecrawl reported "the connected account is low on credits" on every call; the user should top up before further calibration.

Main result: I built an independent known-item set V3 of 18 items. I chose them from domain knowledge, not from the calibration's vocabulary, and all 18 are indexed. Three of the DOIs I first tried resolved to unrelated works and were dropped. Against V3, the calibrated final union retrieves only 11/18 (61%):
- S1 gets 9.
- S6 adds 2.
- S2, S3 and S5 retrieve 0 of the other 7 (tested).
- S4, S7 and S8 cannot retrieve them, because their required title terms are absent (not run).

The misses are classic theory papers and key studies:
- Feder & Regev 1975 (JEEM): pesticide externality and tax model.
- Griffin & Bromley 1982 (AJAE).
- Shortle & Dunn 1986 (AJAE): relative efficiency of nonpoint instruments.
- Shortle & Horan 2001 (J Econ Surveys).
- Antle & Pingali 1994 (AJAE): health versus productivity tradeoff of restricting pesticides.
- Lefebvre et al. 2014: incentives and policies for IPM.
- Mejía, Restrepo & Rozo (WBER, OpenAlex year 2015): suspension of aerial spraying in a border strip as a quasi-experiment.

The tested fixes below retrieve all 7, but that 18/18 is in-sample. The fixes were tuned on V3, so a fresh validation set is needed.

press_items.assessment: The arms map well onto taxes, bans, buffer zones, quotas, information instruments and damage valuation. Two parts of the question are under-translated. (a) A fourth instrument is missing: ex post liability, tort or compensation for drift. That is the standard alternative to ex ante quantity regulation for a spatial externality like aerial drift, and nothing in S1–S8 targets it. (b) The 'which empirical parameter' half of the question (slope of marginal abatement cost via the own-price elasticity of pesticide demand; marginal damage) is reached only indirectly. The final S1 dropped the elasticity terms that the earlier E block carried. Recall claims are optimistic. V2 (12/12) was partly assembled with the same arms, and S-1 (10/10) used the same vocabulary. The independent V3 set gives 11/18.
press_items.suggested_change: Add S9 (drift, liability and compensation) and S10 (demand elasticity and abatement cost). Then build a fresh validation set V4, not used for tuning, for example from the reference lists of Sexton et al. 2007, Finger et al. 2024 and Shortle & Horan 2001, and report recall on it.
press_items.tested: Indexing check: doi:<22 candidate DOIs> returned 21. 10.1016/s0308-521x(00)00007-5 is not indexed. 3 DOIs resolved to unrelated works (10.2307/1242024, 10.2307/1243866, 10.1111/1477-9552.12008) and were dropped, leaving V3 = 18. Recall: doi:<V3> AND S1 = 9 (Kudsk & Mathiassen 2020; Lichtenberg-Spear-Zilberman 1993 reentry; Cropper et al. 1992; Jacquet 2011; Pedersen 2020; Travisi 2006; Sunding & Zivin 2000; Zilberman & Millock 1997; Florax 2005). doi:<9 missed> AND S6 = 2 (Kathage 2017; Brookes 2017). doi:<7 still missed> AND S3 = 0, AND S2 = 0, AND S5 = 0.

press_items.assessment: S3 is over-restrictive. It ANDs 3 title+abstract blocks: an agriculture word, AND instrument/tax/regulation, AND an economics word. It lost 3 of the 3 independent nonpoint classics. Shortle & Horan 2001's OpenAlex abstract says 'economic incentives for nonpoint pollution control ... policy design' and contains no agriculture word and no instrument, tax or regulation word. Griffin & Bromley 1982 has no abstract and depends on the title word 'Externality'. Shortle & Dunn 1986 fails the title block ('Agricultural Source Water Pollution'). Helfand & House was retrieved only because its wording happens to fit.
press_items.suggested_change: S3'' = title.search:(nonpoint OR "non-point" OR "diffuse pollution" OR "diffuse source" OR "agricultural pollution" OR "agricultural runoff" OR "agricultural source"),title_and_abstract.search:(instrument OR instruments OR incentive OR incentives OR tax OR taxes OR taxation OR "second-best" OR "least-cost" OR externality OR externalities OR "water quality trading" OR "pollution trading" OR "permit trading" OR "trading ratio" OR "ambient-based" OR "moral hazard" OR "asymmetric information" OR welfare)
press_items.tested: S3 AND doi:<Shortle-Horan, Griffin-Bromley, Shortle-Dunn> = 0. Broad variant (S3 title + 'agricultural source'; ta = instrument/incentive/tax/regulation/standard/second-best/least-cost/externality/trading/(policy AND econ)) = 1,411, 4/4 including Helfand-House. S3'' = 531, 4/4 (doi:<3 + Helfand-House> = 4). S3'' tail at page 40 (per-page 5, ranks 196–200): 3/5 relevant. Noise comes from 'agricultural sources' of ammonia, and one 'Retracted:' record.

press_items.assessment: S1 sub-blocks miss restriction-framed and tradeoff-framed work. The ban block has no restrict/restriction(s)/'restricted use'. The health sub-arm needs an explicit cost phrase, so Antle & Pingali 1994 is missed: its abstract reads 'policy to restrict pesticide use ... tradeoffs ... social gains'. Lefebvre 2014 is framed as 'incentives and policies'. S6 rescues restriction studies only when they say 'economic impact', 'cost of' and similar. S6 retrieved 2 of 18 independent items that no other arm found, so it must be core, not the first arm cut as the calibration proposed.
press_items.suggested_change: Add the X block to S1's title_and_abstract part: OR (incentive OR incentives OR "policy options" OR "policy mix") OR ((restrict OR restriction OR restrictions OR "restricted use") AND (tradeoff OR tradeoffs OR "trade-off" OR "social gains" OR "social benefits" OR welfare OR productivity OR profit OR "net returns")). Promote S6 to core.
press_items.tested: title.search:(P++ OR NEW),title_and_abstract.search:(X NOT I_S1) = 553 incremental records. doi:<Antle-Pingali, Lefebvre> on the same filter = 2/2. Top-12 about 7/12 relevant: IPM incentives review; 'High-Resolution Analysis of Pesticide Restrictions Highlights a Need to Balance Trade-offs' 2026; 'Atrazine and Water Quality: An Evaluation of Alternative Policy Options' 1996; 'The Case and Opportunity for Public-Supported Financial Incentives to Implement IPM' 2004. Noise: methyl bromide environmental fate; NAMs safety assessment.

press_items.assessment: OpenAlex has no thesaurus, and the strategy relies only on free text. The natural controlled vocabularies for this question are unavailable: EconLit JEL codes (Q52, Q53, Q57, Q58 environmental policy; Q18 agricultural policy; H23 externalities and Pigouvian taxes; K32 environmental law) and CAB Abstracts descriptors (pesticides; taxes; legislation; buffer zones; spray drift). PubMed MeSH would help the HHP-ban arm.
press_items.suggested_change: If EconLit, CAB Abstracts or AgEcon full search becomes available, run the pesticide concept (P++ plus NEW) AND (JEL Q5* OR H23 OR K32). In PubMed: ("Pesticides"[Mesh] OR "Herbicides"[Mesh] OR "Insecticides"[Mesh]) AND ("Government Regulation"[Mesh] OR "Legislation as Topic"[Mesh] OR "Taxes"[Mesh]). Document that OpenAlex topic or keyword filters were not tested.
press_items.tested: Not tested: no EconLit, CAB or PubMed count access in this session.

press_items.assessment:
The pesticide title block (P++) misses several synonyms:
- 'agrichemical(s)': a different word from 'agrochemical'; stemming does not join them.
- 'pest control' and 'pest management'/IPM.
- Bare 'plant protection' (only the phrases 'plant protection product' and 'crop protection' are listed).
- 'biocide' and 'chemical input(s)'.
- Molecules central to this thesis or to drift externalities: procymidone, mancozeb, chlorothalonil, carbofuran, carbaryl (banana/Chapada do Apodi), chlordecone (banana, Caribbean), dicamba (drift), and the neonicotinoid active ingredients imidacloprid, clothianidin and thiamethoxam. Also fipronil, aldicarb, parathion and lindane.
These omissions cost Feder & Regev 1975, whose title says 'economics of pest control'.
press_items.suggested_change: NEW = "pest control" OR "pest management" OR "plant protection" OR agrichemical OR agrichemicals OR "agri-chemical" OR "agro-chemical" OR biocide OR nematicide OR acaricide OR mancozeb OR procymidone OR chlorothalonil OR carbofuran OR carbaryl OR dicamba OR aldicarb OR chlordecone OR parathion OR lindane OR fipronil OR imidacloprid OR clothianidin OR thiamethoxam OR "chemical input" OR "chemical inputs". OR it into the title blocks of S1, S6 and S7.
press_items.tested: title.search:(NEW NOT P++),title_and_abstract.search:(I_S1) = 194 new records. Top-10 mostly on topic, e.g. 'Impacts of taxes to reduce agrichemical use when farm policy is endogenous' (1994), 'Market approval, tax and incentive to invest in R&D on agrichemical markets' (2015), 'Agricultural insurance, premium subsidies and chemical inputs' (2026). doi:<Feder-Regev, Lefebvre> on the same filter = 1 (Feder & Regev).

press_items.assessment: Drift, liability and compensation, the missing fourth instrument, has a compact, high-yield vocabulary.
press_items.suggested_change: S9 = title_and_abstract.search:(("spray drift" OR "pesticide drift" OR "herbicide drift" OR "dicamba drift" OR "drift damage" OR "drift injury" OR "drift complaints") AND (liability OR compensation OR economic OR economics OR welfare OR externality OR externalities OR "cost-benefit" OR lawsuit OR litigation OR "damage claims"))
press_items.tested: S9 = 165. S9 AND S1 = 12, so S9 adds about 153. Top-12 includes 'Assigning liability for pesticide spray drift' (2013), 'Tort tradeoffs in cases of pesticide drift: A legal and economic analysis' (2022), 'Creating a compensation program for injuries from dicamba spray drift and volatilization' (2021), 'Improvements in pesticide drift reduction technology (DRT) call for improving liability provisions' (2017), 'Potential Economic Impacts of Draft Restrictions to Address Pesticide Drift and Runoff: Rice' (2012), 'Chemical Trespass? ... Efforts To Control Pesticide Drift' (1985) and 'Spatial arrangements of externality generating and receiving activities' (2003). Noise: remote sensing of drift injury. An earlier draft containing 'off-target' was not run; 'off-target' is generic (genetics) and should be avoided.

press_items.assessment: S4 requires the aerial term in the TITLE. It therefore misses economics papers where aerial spraying appears only in the abstract, such as Mejía, Restrepo & Rozo (WBER): the suspension of aerial spraying in a strip near the Ecuador border, effectively a buffer-zone natural experiment.
press_items.suggested_change: Keep S4 and add S4b = title_and_abstract.search:(("aerial spraying" OR "aerial fumigation" OR "aerial eradication" OR "aerial spray" OR "aerial application" OR "aerial herbicide" OR "aerially sprayed" OR "aerially applied" OR "crop dusting" OR "pulverização aérea" OR "fumigación aérea" OR "aspersión aérea") AND (ban OR banned OR banning OR suspension OR suspended OR prohibition OR prohibited OR "buffer zone" OR "natural experiment" OR "quasi-experiment" OR "quasi-experimental" OR "difference-in-differences" OR "regression discontinuity" OR "exogenous variation" OR welfare OR externality OR externalities OR "cost-benefit")). Consider adding "aviação agrícola" (untested).
press_items.tested: S4b = 290. doi:<Mejía 2015, Camacho & Mejía 2017, EU aerial ban 2018> AND S4b = 2 (Mejía; EU ban). Camacho & Mejía remains covered by S4. Top-10 about 5/10 relevant, including 'A 50 m Buffer Zone to Protect Humans and Ecosystems From Pesticide Aerial Spray Drift: Is It Enough?' (2006) and 'Buffer zone widths for honeybees from ground and aerial spraying' (1990). These are physical drift-distance damage relations, relevant to buffer width. Noise: AgDISP model, a 1939 spray-mixture note. S4b ∩ S4 was not measured.

press_items.assessment: The parameter side of the question (own-price elasticity of pesticide demand as the slope of marginal abatement cost under a tax) is not targeted. The 'damage function' wording does not translate into a usable arm. In pesticide economics, 'damage function' and 'damage threshold' mostly mean pest damage-control or economic-injury-level concepts, not external marginal damage.
press_items.suggested_change: S10 = title.search:(P++ OR NEW),title_and_abstract.search:("price elasticity" OR "demand elasticity" OR "elasticity of demand" OR "own-price" OR elasticities OR "price response" OR "price responsiveness" OR "demand for pesticides" OR "pesticide demand" OR "marginal abatement cost" OR "abatement cost"). Narrowing bare 'elasticity' to these phrases is untested. Do not add a standalone damage-function arm. Instead, tell screeners about the damage-control versus external-damage ambiguity.
press_items.tested: title.search:P++, ta:((elasticity OR elasticities OR "price response" OR "price responsiveness" OR "demand for pesticides" OR "pesticide demand" OR "marginal abatement cost" OR "abatement cost") NOT I_S1) = 170 incremental. Top-12 8/12 relevant (own-price elasticity meta-analysis and its dataset; 'Disaggregating the Demand for Pesticides' 2015; 'Farm Programs and Pesticide Demand' 1991; 'Estimation of price elasticities for components of fertilizers and pesticides' 2000). Noise: 2 records on the elasticity of apple flesh under methyl bromide. Damage-function arm: title.search:P++, ta:(("damage function(s)" OR "dose-response" OR "dose response" OR "marginal damage(s)" OR "exposure-response" OR "concentration-response" OR "nonlinear damage" OR "convex damage" OR "damage threshold") AND (economic OR ... OR "social optimum")) = 91. Top-12 about 1/12 relevant (herbicide efficacy dose-response, OECD 216, toxicology), so rejected.

press_items.assessment: Buffer-zone vocabulary: S2 correctly avoids bare 'setback'. Bare 'no-spray' and 'buffer strip' are also hazardous: they pull in agronomic untreated-control and profitability trials. S2's pesticide block has no fumigant terms, but the US soil-fumigant buffer-zone literature is titled by fumigant, not 'pesticide'. Other small gaps: 'Pigovian' (S1 lists only 'Pigouvian'); 'tradeable' (British spelling, which the stemmer does not map to 'tradable'); fee(s), charge(s), excise; French 'phytosanitaire(s)' and 'redevance' (the French pesticide levy, which is explicitly in scope).
press_items.suggested_change: In S2-A3b's pesticide block add fumigant OR fumigants OR fumigation OR "methyl bromide" OR dichloropropene OR chloropicrin. In S1-I add Pigovian OR "tradeable permit" OR fee OR fees OR excise OR "pollution charge" OR redevance. In the title block add phytosanitaire OR phytosanitaires. All of these are untested and should be measured before adoption.
press_items.tested: BUF variant: title.search:(P++ OR drift), ta:(("buffer strip(s)" OR setback(s) OR "buffer distance" OR "buffer width" OR "buffer zone" OR "no-spray" OR "spray-free" OR "pesticide-free zone") AND (cost-benefit/economic impact/compensation/welfare/WTP/net returns/profit...)) = 887. Top-12 about 4/12 relevant; noise is fungicide-profitability and drone-spraying papers. Rejected; keep S2's phrase-limited terms. The fumigant and spelling additions were not run.

press_items.assessment:
Verified OpenAlex behaviours relevant to this design:
1. NOT is honoured inside a single title.search or title_and_abstract.search value (the x_query shows is_negated on every term). The calibration's claim that overlaps can only be measured by AND-ing therefore understates what is possible: exact within-field increments can be measured.
2. 6 of 18 V3 records have has_abstract:false (Lefebvre, Jacquet, Griffin-Bromley, Feder-Regev, Travisi, Zilberman-Millock). S1 still matched 3 of them on words that are not in their titles, so OpenAlex appears to search some abstracts it does not display. Records with truly absent abstracts reduce to title-only matching, which is why the 1975–1982 classics fail the instrument block.
3. Weitzman 1974 is a single record (W1525260320, cited_by_count 2,815), so S5 is not split across duplicates.
4. Backward chasing (cited_by:) from Fernandez-Cornejo 1998, Shortle-Horan 2001 and Finger 2024 returned 84 references but 0 of the 7 V3 misses. OpenAlex reference lists for older JSTOR records are incomplete.
5. Untested caution: commas separate OpenAlex filters, so '2,4-D' or '1,3-D' cannot be written inside a filter value; use 'dichlorophenoxyacetic', 'dichloropropene' or 'Telone'.
press_items.suggested_change: Use within-field NOT to report exact increments for S6, S7 and S10 against S1 (all share the title P block). Do not rely on OpenAlex backward chasing for pre-1990 classics; hand-check the reference lists of 2–3 review seeds instead. Avoid comma-containing molecule names.
press_items.tested: doi:<V3>,has_abstract:false = 6. title.search:"prices vs quantities",publication_year:1973-1975 = 1. cited_by:W2122461934|W4391836656|W2003263487 = 84; AND doi:<7 misses> = 0. NOT increments: NEW NOT P++ = 194; X NOT I = 553; E NOT I = 170.

press_items.assessment: No date or type limits is correct, since the seeds span 1974–2024 and the classics are pre-1990. The revision raises volume: S1 +747 (194 + 553), S3 +357 (531 instead of 174), S4b up to +290, S9 about +153, S10 about +170. That is roughly +1,700 gross before overlaps, taking OpenAlex from about 3,600–3,800 to about 5,000–5,500 before deduplication. A 'Retracted:' record appeared in the S3'' tail. Adding the 7 V3 misses raised V3 recall from 11/18 to 18/18, but that figure is in-sample.
press_items.suggested_change: Add type:!paratext and drop is_retracted:true records at deduplication (counts untested). Screen in this order: S1 core, S2, S3'', S6, S9, S4/S4b, S5, S7, S10, S8, then the S1 X-block increment, which is the costliest, about 1/3 noise in its top-12, and suits AI-prioritized screening. Validate on a fresh V4 set before freezing the protocol.
press_items.tested: Not run: type/retraction filter counts. Volume figures are the sums of the measured counts listed above, not a single union call.

recommended_final_query:
Run every OpenAlex arm with no date or type limit. Keep S2, S5, S7 and S8 as calibrated. Change S1 and S3, promote S6 to core, and add S4b, S9 and S10.

Definitions:
- P++ = S1's title block as calibrated.
- NEW = "pest control" OR "pest management" OR "plant protection" OR agrichemical OR agrichemicals OR "agri-chemical" OR "agro-chemical" OR biocide OR nematicide OR acaricide OR mancozeb OR procymidone OR chlorothalonil OR carbofuran OR carbaryl OR dicamba OR aldicarb OR chlordecone OR parathion OR lindane OR fipronil OR imidacloprid OR clothianidin OR thiamethoxam OR "chemical input" OR "chemical inputs"
- I = S1's title_and_abstract block as calibrated.
- X = (incentive OR incentives OR "policy options" OR "policy mix") OR ((restrict OR restriction OR restrictions OR "restricted use") AND (tradeoff OR tradeoffs OR "trade-off" OR "social gains" OR "social benefits" OR welfare OR productivity OR profit OR "net returns"))

Arms:

S1' (about 2,292, the sum of disjoint measured parts 1,545 + 194 + 553):
filter=title.search:(P++ OR NEW),title_and_abstract.search:(I OR X)

S2 (689): unchanged. Add fumigant/fumigation/dichloropropene/chloropicrin to the A3b pesticide block (untested).

S3'' (531):
filter=title.search:(nonpoint OR "non-point" OR "diffuse pollution" OR "diffuse source" OR "agricultural pollution" OR "agricultural runoff" OR "agricultural source"),title_and_abstract.search:(instrument OR instruments OR incentive OR incentives OR tax OR taxes OR taxation OR "second-best" OR "least-cost" OR externality OR externalities OR "water quality trading" OR "pollution trading" OR "permit trading" OR "trading ratio" OR "ambient-based" OR "moral hazard" OR "asymmetric information" OR welfare)

S4 (227): unchanged.

S4b (290):
filter=title_and_abstract.search:(("aerial spraying" OR "aerial fumigation" OR "aerial eradication" OR "aerial spray" OR "aerial application" OR "aerial herbicide" OR "aerially sprayed" OR "aerially applied" OR "crop dusting" OR "pulverização aérea" OR "fumigación aérea" OR "aspersión aérea") AND (ban OR banned OR banning OR suspension OR suspended OR prohibition OR prohibited OR "buffer zone" OR "natural experiment" OR "quasi-experiment" OR "quasi-experimental" OR "difference-in-differences" OR "regression discontinuity" OR "exogenous variation" OR welfare OR externality OR externalities OR "cost-benefit"))

S5 (108): unchanged.
filter=cites:W1525260320,title_and_abstract.search:(<agricultural block>)

S6 (core, about 740): change the title block to (P++ OR NEW). Do not cut this arm.

S7 (189): change the first title block to (P++ OR NEW).

S8 (391): unchanged.

S9 (165; about 153 not in S1):
filter=title_and_abstract.search:(("spray drift" OR "pesticide drift" OR "herbicide drift" OR "dicamba drift" OR "drift damage" OR "drift injury" OR "drift complaints") AND (liability OR compensation OR economic OR economics OR welfare OR externality OR externalities OR "cost-benefit" OR lawsuit OR litigation OR "damage claims"))

S10 (about 170 beyond S1, measured with P++ title and bare 'elasticity'):
filter=title.search:(P++ OR NEW),title_and_abstract.search:("price elasticity" OR "demand elasticity" OR "elasticity of demand" OR "own-price" OR elasticities OR "price response" OR "price responsiveness" OR "demand for pesticides" OR "pesticide demand" OR "marginal abatement cost" OR "abatement cost")

Also:
- Hand-add Weitzman 1974 (W1525260320).
- Untested small additions: S1-I += Pigovian OR "tradeable permit" OR fee OR fees OR excise OR "pollution charge" OR redevance; title block += phytosanitaire OR phytosanitaires.
- Estimated volume: about 5,000–5,500 gross before deduplication; add type:!paratext and drop retracted records.
- Validate on a fresh set V4 before freezing, because V3 recall (18/18) is in-sample.
missing_concepts_or_synonyms: ex post liability / tort / compensation for drift (a fourth instrument, absent)
spray drift / pesticide drift / herbicide drift / dicamba drift
own-price elasticity of pesticide demand / pesticide demand / marginal abatement cost (the parameter a tax needs)
agrichemical / agrichemicals (not joined to 'agrochemical' by stemming)
pest control / pest management / integrated pest management (IPM)
bare 'plant protection'
restrict / restriction / restrictions / restricted use (missing from the S1 ban block)
incentive / incentives / policy options / policy mix
tradeoff / tradeoffs / social gains (health-productivity framing, e.g. Antle & Pingali 1994)
molecules: procymidone, mancozeb, chlorothalonil, carbofuran, carbaryl, chlordecone, dicamba, imidacloprid, clothianidin, thiamethoxam, fipronil, aldicarb, parathion, lindane
chemical input / chemical inputs; biocide; nematicide; acaricide
fumigant / fumigation / dichloropropene / chloropicrin in the buffer-zone arm (soil-fumigant buffer zones)
'agricultural source' (nonpoint title synonym, e.g. Shortle & Dunn 1986)
nonpoint instrument-design terms: incentives, moral hazard, asymmetric information, ambient-based, trading ratio, water quality trading
aerial spraying suspension / quasi-experiment in the abstract (not only the title)
Pigovian (S1 lists only the 'Pigouvian' spelling)
tradeable permit (British spelling)
fee / fees / excise / pollution charge / redevance (French pesticide levy)
phytosanitaire(s) (French)
aviação agrícola (PT)
JEL Q52/Q58/H23/K32 and CAB descriptors (controlled vocabulary not available)
